unit: K (kelvin), mean absolute error of Tg
tuned_trees_config: GradientBoostingRegressor(n_estimators=300, max_depth=4, learning_rate=0.1, subsample=0.8, random_state=42). It won 8 configurations on 3-fold grouped CV over training rows only, using the folds in tasks.json cv0-cv2, which I checked are subsets of the training rows with no shared group. CV MAE was 15.22 K for the winner and 15.89 K for the fixed config. I scored the winner once on test: 16.37 K.
safe_sentence: We held out whole copolymer systems the model never saw (152 of 666 measured rows). On those rows our from-scratch JavaScript neural network predicts glass-transition temperature with an average error of 15.3 K. Guessing the average gives 66 K, and gradient-boosted trees give 16.4 to 17.5 K. The error is about 6 K on real copolymers and about 30 K on pure homopolymers.
unsafe_sentence: Do not say: "Our neural network predicts the Tg of any new polymer to within 15 K and clearly beats tree-based machine learning." The error is about 30 K on homopolymers and 18.5 K when a monomer is unseen. The edge over trees is about 1 K, and over 8 overlapping splits the trees won 2 of 8. Also do not say it was trained on the Hugging Face homopolymer set. That set was not used (0 rows).
verdict:
The result reproduces and I found no leak. I trained their 5-member ensemble ([128,64], 200 epochs, huber, decay 0.01, lr 0.004, seed 11) on W/nn_data.json with their trainer and scored it with my own code. Test MAE was 15.33 K, the same as claimed. The naive mean was 66.44 K and the fixed trees 17.54 K, both matching.

Leak audit:
(a) Input and target standardisation in nn_generic.js uses training rows only, and there is no clipping. The Fox and homopolymer-Tg inputs are built only from training rows (matrix(..., tr)), leaving out the row's own group.
(b) No group id is on both sides of the split. Pairs are stored in sorted order, and no unordered monomer pair appears on both sides. No test input vector is identical to a training one. No test homopolymer has the same pure monomer as a training row, including the 14 pure endpoint rows inside copolymer groups. The Hugging Face homopolymer file was not used for training (0 rows).
(c) Settings, ensemble size and the Morgan-feature choice were all chosen by grouped CV on training rows. Test tracking is off (track:false), and there is no early stopping on test.
(d) No Calculated or Calulated column is read. prepare.py reads only the SMILES, comp_0 and Tg(K) columns.
(e) The seeded() helper and the Mlp class are byte-identical to /workspace/ncsu-hackathon/src/lib/nn.js (diff is empty). The network has no trees, lookups, pre-trained weights or imports.

Fair fight: the CV-tuned trees scored 16.37 K, so the network still wins on the main split by about 1.0 K. On the 8 extra grouped splits, using their network predictions from runs/final.json, the network beat the tuned trees on 6 of 8. The mean difference was -0.99 K (95% t interval -1.85 to -0.13), but the splits overlap, so the interval is too narrow. Their own report says the same thing for the fixed trees.

Caveats:
- The error depends heavily on the subset: about 5.8 K on 93 true-copolymer test rows, but 30.3 K on 59 homopolymer test rows, and 18.5 K on their split with unseen monomers.
- The main split comes from GroupShuffleSplit(seed 42). It is a single split of a small dataset.

My scripts are in W/verify: rerun.mjs, score.py, audit.py, tune.py and splits8.py.
